transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Before I finalize the approval on the six-week peer-feedback pilot, I want to do our standard round-robin check-in with both the project team member and our HR program partner. I'd like to hear any thoughts or concerns about the pilot as currently described -- and specifically, I want to make sure we're all aligned on the operating safeguards we'll put in place. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I want to share something I've observed that I think is directly relevant to the safeguards discussion. Over the last three retrospectives, I personally witnessed exactly five dismissive interruptions. Separately, two colleagues who were affected told me they would only contribute feedback through an anonymous written channel going forward rather than speaking up in the group. I think this is important context for designing the right safeguards for the pilot.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thanks, Elena. I need to flag something important before we finalize. I confirmed with HR this morning that because this pilot follows repeated conduct concerns, specific safeguards are required: the pilot must be opt-in for all participants, it must use an independent neutral facilitator, participants must sign a written non-retaliation acknowledgment, and we must conduct a documented review exactly 30 days after launch. This guidance came in after the current draft circulated, so it hasn't been added to the proposal yet. These aren't optional -- they're required conditions for the pilot to proceed.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both. This is exactly why we do this round-robin before finalizing. Darius, the pattern you're describing -- five dismissive interruptions across three retrospectives and colleagues already pulling back to anonymous-only channels -- tells me the current draft's safeguards are not sufficient for the environment we're actually operating in. Mei, the HR guidance you're bringing is clear and binding. Let me make sure I'm capturing everything correctly before I issue the final plan. The pilot will proceed, but only with these conditions incorporated: First, participation will be opt-in for all participants -- no one is required to participate. Second, we will use an independent neutral facilitator, not someone internal to the team. Third, all participants will sign a written non-retaliation acknowledgment before the pilot begins. Fourth, we will conduct a documented review exactly 30 days after launch, in addition to the end-of-pilot review already described. Darius, I also want the observed interruption pattern noted as part of the pilot's context documentation so the facilitator is aware. Does either of you see any gaps before I finalize this?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I don't see any gaps. The conditions you've laid out -- opt-in participation, an independent neutral facilitator, the written non-retaliation acknowledgment, and the 30-day documented review -- directly address the concerns I raised. And documenting the interruption pattern so the facilitator is aware is important. I'm comfortable with this approach. One thing I'd emphasize: given that two colleagues have already said they'll only contribute through anonymous written channels, I'd want to make sure the opt-in structure and the anonymous channel option are clearly communicated to everyone before the pilot launches, so people know there's a safe way to participate without having to ask for it.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Darius, that's a great point about clearly communicating the opt-in structure and anonymous channel option upfront. I'd add that the non-retaliation acknowledgment itself should explicitly reference the anonymous written channel as a protected way to participate, so people understand that choosing anonymity is covered under the non-retaliation commitment. I'm satisfied that the four HR-required conditions plus Elena's addition of documenting the interruption pattern cover the necessary safeguards. Elena, I don't see any gaps -- I'm comfortable with you finalizing this.
transcript.speaker: A3

Conduct a documented review exactly 30 days after launch in addition to the end-of-pilot review already described in the proposal.
